title: The Research & Infrastructure Trail
subtitle: OpenCog · Novamente · Southern Trust
description: Source-linked examination of a 2012 informatics proposal, 2015 AI/genomics software invoice, attempted server setup, and later conflicting litigation accounts. Architectural ornament comparisons remain explicitly separate.

sources.title: OpenCog humanoid robotics proposal
sources.note: Proposal describes a Hong Kong AI robotics project and requested funding. A proposal does not establish payment.

sources.title: January grant follow-up correspondence
sources.note: Discusses a delayed contribution. This record does not itself prove a completed transfer.

sources.title: Southern Trust payment-route email
sources.note: Accountant discusses a prior January 2014 payment and a proposed additional payment.

sources.title: Novamente genomics-analysis invoice
sources.note: Invoice names Southern Trust and describes machine-learning analysis of gene-expression and SNP data. Payment and delivery require separate evidence.

sources.title: Virgin Islands server access discussion
sources.note: Email discusses difficulty remotely installing software on a server because router access was not configured.

sources.title: OpenCog Simple Deception specification
sources.note: Technical research example about an agent reasoning about another agent's beliefs. Does not establish deployed harmful use.

sources.title: Lexi-style architectural onlay catalog
sources.note: Commercial catalog reference. Catalog publication date is unknown; visual similarity is not provenance or affiliation.

sources.title: Virtual animals integrated cognitive architecture proposal
sources.note: Describes a proposed research budget, not a verified award or completed project.

sources.title: Court-filed expert review of 2012 EDC testimony
sources.note: Expert report prepared for JPMorgan's counsel, filed in August 2023. It cites 2012 testimony and the Southern Trust application claiming proposed DNA database and informatics work; this is a party-retained expert opinion, not a judicial finding.

sources.title: Request and discussion of DNA-database software invoice
sources.note: Feb 3 request specifies algorithmic DNA database management. Feb 5 accountant asks whether to pay immediately or wait for servers and software. Does not establish payment or delivery.

sources.title: USVI amended complaint concerning Southern Trust
sources.note: Litigating government's allegations about Southern Trust's informatics business and tax incentives. Allegations are not findings of fact or proof that no experimental AI equipment existed.

sources.title: Secondary report citing alleged April 2015 accounting ledger entry
sources.note: Secondary research text reports an April 13, 2015 $30,000 Novamente entry and cites EFTA00809214. The original ledger page and document identifier attribution remain unconfirmed; this source record denotes a research lead, not a verified bank transaction.

hypotheses.question: Was the February 2015 genomics software delivered and used?
hypotheses.context: An itemized invoice and separate access correspondence make this question testable, but neither is a deployment record.
hypotheses.forEvidence: Invoice describes software, installation and training services.
hypotheses.againstEvidence: No verified installation log, acceptance record or matching payment confirmation in the seeded documents.
hypotheses.nextCheck: Seek bank confirmation, inventory, signed acceptance, and deployment logs.

hypotheses.question: Did the remote server process genetic datasets?
hypotheses.context: A genomics-related invoice and an AI-server email concern the same broad research environment but do not establish a shared workload.
hypotheses.forEvidence: Both records involve software work and infrastructure during 2015.
hypotheses.againstEvidence: No host identifiers, data inventory, dataset access records or application logs are linked.
hypotheses.nextCheck: Match host asset identifiers and documented application/data provenance.

hypotheses.question: Does the exact three-loop ornament recur at connected properties?
hypotheses.context: The ornamental photograph motivated this atlas. Broad decorative similarities are not exact matches.
hypotheses.forEvidence: Historically inspired onlays repeat similar curls and floral forms.
hypotheses.againstEvidence: No matching maker, mold, construction record or independently confirmed duplicate has been established.
hypotheses.nextCheck: Compare normalized contours and original architectural catalog plates, with dated provenance.

hypotheses.question: Which proposed AI grants were actually paid?
hypotheses.context: Correspondence includes requested amounts, payment-route changes, and research proposals.
hypotheses.forEvidence: The documents show negotiated contributions and retrospective payment references.
hypotheses.againstEvidence: A proposal, invoice, or authorization is not a completed bank settlement.
hypotheses.nextCheck: Reconcile grant agreements, receiving-party accounts, and transaction confirmations.

hypotheses.question: Was Southern Trust's proposed DNA database ever operated?
hypotheses.context: A 2012 proposal, a 2015 software invoice, and a later legal dispute are linked by company and topic, but not by operational logs.
hypotheses.forEvidence: A 2015 commercial invoice describes concrete genetic-data analysis software services.
hypotheses.againstEvidence: The Feb 5 payment question and June router problem leave payment, delivery and operation unresolved; USVI later disputed the represented business.
hypotheses.nextCheck: Find vendor acceptance records, server inventories, data provenance, application logs, and case-resolved findings.

traceSteps.title: A planned biomedical and financial informatics business
traceSteps.established: A court-filed expert report cites Southern Trust's application and Epstein's 2012 EDC testimony describing a proposed DNA database, medical analysis and financial algorithms.
traceSteps.notEstablished: That a DNA database was actually built, populated with data, or used commercially.

traceSteps.title: An algorithmic DNA-database invoice was requested
traceSteps.established: Kahn requested an invoice from Goertzel for algorithmic DNA database management billed to Southern Trust.
traceSteps.notEstablished: A finalized software delivery, operational database, or payment.

traceSteps.title: Novamente issued a $30,000 software-and-services invoice
traceSteps.established: An invoice describes machine learning and automated reasoning for gene-expression and SNP analysis, plus installation and training.
traceSteps.notEstablished: That the invoice was paid, that the work was delivered, or that the system was functional.

traceSteps.title: Payment was explicitly still being discussed
traceSteps.established: Kahn asked whether to send $30,000 immediately or wait for server delivery and software availability in an estimated two or three weeks.
traceSteps.notEstablished: That the funds were transferred, servers arrived, or software was installed.

traceSteps.title: Remote installation was described as unsuccessful
traceSteps.established: Goertzel wrote that his team had not been able to install software on a Virgin Islands server because remote router access remained unavailable.
traceSteps.notEstablished: That the same machine related to the February invoice or that installation succeeded later.

traceSteps.title: The Virgin Islands disputed the claimed commercial informatics activity
traceSteps.established: The USVI filed allegations that Southern Trust did not operate the informatics business it described when seeking tax incentives.
traceSteps.notEstablished: A court adjudication of every alleged fact or proof that no experimental software or server was ever present.

traceSteps.title: A court-filed report reviewed the 2012 proposal and oversight
traceSteps.established: A JPMorgan-retained expert reviewed EDC tax incentives, cited the proposed informatics business, and criticized government examination of its feasibility.
traceSteps.notEstablished: An independently established inventory of the software's later operation or a final judicial conclusion.
